summary: Remove the mismatched supporting citation 69/81; retain prs 112/34.
rationale: 69/81 actually has affirmative disclosure of a king’s son and a question who disclosed it, not the quoted reciprocal refusal. The latter matches supplied PrS 41/5.

summary: l-maxlūq is the recipient under negation, not the person betrayed.
before: I would not betray God’s creature
after: Ich werde es keinem Geschöpf Gottes verraten!
rationale: 47/44 edition German explicitly reads keinem Geschöpf Gottes; the recurrent l-recipient contrasts with ʕal marking the target of denunciation.

summary: Translate not revealing the secret to anyone, rather than betraying a creature
before: I would not betray God’s creature
after: I will not reveal it to any creature of God
rationale: In lə=ko-maqənno l-maxlūq d-aloho, l-maxlūq is the recipient of disclosure. At 47/39–44 the priest fears being exposed and the shepherd promises not to tell anyone. The edition explicitly translates “Ich werde es keinem Geschöpf Gottes verraten!”, not a promise not to betray a creature as the object.

summary: maqəlle d-i=duġriye is confession, not festsetzen.
rationale: PrS 83/67 supplies the same clause with a truthful admission; compare existing youngest-brother confession under 2 and PrS 64/43.

summary: File the confession of the truth under sense 2
rationale: The Turoyo maqəlle d-i=duġriye and its translation “er hat die Wahrheit gestanden” concern confessing/saying the truth, matching existing sense 2 “verraten, sagen”. They do not mean setting/fixing something, the current sense 1 “festsetzen”. The supplied Prym–Socin passage has the same confession, followed by “do not cut off his head”.

summary: New box ko-Preterit: example for sense 2 in ko-Preterit (103/43)

data.turoyo: <...> W yawma kmaqəllilux, kobaʕno, d baxtux obatli. <...>
data.translation: <...> Heute habe ich es dir gestanden und bitte dich, mir Verzeihung zu gewähren.

rationale: New ko-Preterit box, with 1sg agent and 2sg recipient.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (JTM 5.1/38)

data.turoyo: <...> malle ḥzay məs səmle ṭər maqər gənnaḥle, d lə maqər lə knaḥle!
data.translation: <...> Sag ihm ... schau, was er getan hat, das soll er gestehen, dann wird er genesen. Wenn er nicht gesteht, wird er nicht genesen.

rationale: Fills Infectum 2 from four to five; explicit confession under a condition.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (Talay 2/10)

data.turoyo: <...> bətr me d hawi ṭayo, maqəlle ʕal i xəznaṯe w məlle: "Kito xəzna d kṯowe, e, kito xəzna harke, mak koḏaʕ, mək kito eba." <...>
data.translation: <...> Nachdem er Muslim geworden war, hat dieser dieses Versteck (lit.: Schatz) verraten. Er sagte: Es gibt einen Bücherschatz, nein, es gibt hier einen Schatz, wer weiß, was sich darin befindet! <...>

rationale: After moving the inherited confession to 2, fills Preterit 2 to five; ʕal marks disclosed topic, not denounced person.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (36/117)

data.turoyo: L nošo lo məllele, u Silo lo maqərle.
data.translation: Niemand sagte etwas, und Silo verriet nichts.

rationale: Unusual retained r before the Preterit l-agent, contrasting inherited assimilated maqəlle.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (47/39)

data.translation: "Hm!" sprach der Pfarrer, "bei Gott, du wirst mich verraten."

rationale: Clear cross-box government contrast: ʕal target of denunciation versus inherited l-recipient.

summary: Sense 2: revise the gloss
rationale: Explicitly includes confession of the truth, which the source verse and an existing sense-2 confession example support; no change to sense 1 festsetzen.

summary: All 46 tokens fit III disclosure or confession. The inherited truth-confession example is moved from 1 to 2; festsetzen remains numbered 1 without inventing a new attestation.
l- marks a recipient, including pronominal suffixes; ʕal can mark the person denounced or the topic disclosed. The recipient interpretation at 47/44 corrects an existing mistranslation.

r+l assimilation gives maqəlle, while 36/117 retains maqərle. MAC emphatic-lateral forms are compatible with the same root, but bare maqəḷḷe can resemble recipient-suffixed Infectum and is not promoted as secure contrasting morphology.
g-/k- forms may express secrecy commitments, predictions and counterfactual consequences without -wa. The existing 47/40 Infectum-wa is already quoted; 103/43 adds ko-Preterit.

PrS verse references correspond to inherited page/line citations in several duplicate passages. Only the demonstrably wrong 69/81 supporting reference is removed; its affirmative actual passage is documented here rather than substituted into the reciprocal quote.
Round 2 only. Jan English is a project machine translation; semantic decisions are based on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals remain prior material and are not re-proposed here.
No new stem, box, sense, idiom or inherited correction. Retained r in maqərle is already exemplified in round 1 at 36/117.

The subject switch follows morphology: plural captors seize and beat, singular -le reveals, then plural azzən resumes the captors. The supplied English is compatible but does not establish these roles independently.
Jan adds no support for festsetzen (III.1); preserve its inherited number without re-proposing round-1 gloss or correction.
Confirm whether MAC Mother Mary/16,24 maqəḷḷe is Preterit or recipient-suffixed Infectum; no example addition depends on that distinction.
Resolve lo+maqi<rutu> in MAC Old lady/38 and gmaqəllalux in 58/277 against the source/paradigm.
Supply the edition translation of the disclosure clause at PrS 64/23 and any authentic Ritter translation for 69/177 before quoting them.
Does festsetzen have independent support beyond the misfiled inherited confession? This batch supplies none; retain its existing label pending editorial review.
Confirm the singular revealer and recoverable disclosure content at Jan 2.14/3403; this verse does not state an overt content argument.
A personified throne discloses information to the queen; participant extension of telling, not a new sense.
Jan supports round-1 explicit gestehen: maqərle follows seizure and beating, with singular revealer after plural captors. The cave location is contextually recoverable, not an overt verb object.
